learning_outcomes.text: Systematically design a complex electrotechnical system from functional requirements.
Divide a system into coherent hardware and software modules and specify the interfaces between these modules.
Apply models and methods from different electrotechnical disciplines in the design of a practical system.
Design, implement, and test electronic circuits, control engineering algorithms, embedded/real-time software, computer vision algorithms, and cryptographic modules.
Develop measurement and test methods to evaluate the performance of individual modules and of the integrated system.
Integrate various technical modules into a working system and systematically analyze and solve integration problems.
Substantiate design choices based on theoretical models, experimental results, and technical constraints.
Plan and execute a technical project in a team, with a clear division of tasks and mutual coordination.
Communicate technical results, design choices, and problems clearly verbally and in writing.
Critically reflect on one's own contribution, the functioning of the team, and the quality of the realized system.

syllabus_topics: Design of an autonomously driving car (scale 1:10)
Localization system based on infrared beacons (analog and digital electronics)
Controller for navigation and lane-keeping (control engineering and real-time software)
Image processing algorithms for localization and recognition of traffic signs (image processing and machine learning)
Cryptographic module for decoding instruction codes (cryptography and hardware acceleration)
Wireless power transfer via coils under the car (power electronics)
assessment_rules: Students are assessed by their project leaders, supporting academic staff, and peers throughout the year. Points are awarded for teamwork and individual presentations. The technical-scientific quality of the final result is always decisive in determining the final score. For resits, a new assignment is defined per student to demonstrate the required level.
